1 شَبِقَ , (S, M, O, Msb, K,) aor.
شَبَقَ , (Msb, K,) inf. n. شَبَقٌ, (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb,) He was, or became, affected with vehement lust, or carnal desire: (S, M, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) said of a man; (M, Msb;) and in like manner one says of a woman; and also, sometimes, of other than human beings. (M, TA.) ―
-b2- And شَبِقَ مِنَ اللَّحْمِ He suffered indigestion, or turned away with disgust, from flesh-meat. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
